rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so the first experiment should establish a baseline. Testing an RNA-only model with PCA encoding (config_001) clarifies the performance of a simple, single-modality approach. This reduces uncertainty about the baseline accuracy and helps determine if multimodal approaches (which are more complex) might offer significant improvements.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only singleprofile with PCA encoding achieves 0.48 validation accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (same RNA encoder, no image encoder), isolating the effect of profile settings and aggregation. It balances exploration of multiprofile (which may capture more data) with a simple aggregation method, avoiding simultaneous changes to multiple components. This clarifies whether multiprofile or aggregation improves performance, both critical design choices with limited prior evidence.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile RNA-only models (config_002) outperform singleprofile (config_001). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool (config_002) with transformer aggregation improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It balances exploration of key design choices while building on the promising multiprofile direction.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (config_002, 0.5906 accuracy) outperforms singleprofile and transformer aggregation. This experiment tests replacing pca_n2000 with scvi_n200 RNA encoder in the same multiprofile/avgpool setup to isolate the impact of RNA encoder choice. It balances exploitation of the promising multiprofile direction with exploration of encoder variations, which could reveal if scvi_n200 improves performance further.

The existing evidence shows that config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6501). This experiment tests whether adding image data (multimodal) with the same RNA encoder and aggregation method could further improve performance. It isolates the effect of multimodal fusion while building on the proven effectiveness of scvi_n200 and avgpool, balancing exploration and exploitation.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with multiprofile and avgpool aggregation achieves 0.650124 accuracy (config_005), but multimodal approaches like config_030 (0.631518) lag behind. This experiment tests transformer aggregation (vs. avgpool in config_030) with concat fusion, isolating the effect of aggregation method on multimodal performance. It balances exploration of aggregation improvements and exploitation of the strong scvi_n200 RNA encoder, while avoiding redundant changes to multiple design choices.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, and transformer aggregation achieve high validation accuracy (0.6878). This experiment tests whether switching from concat to weighted fusion (a critical design choice) could further improve performance. It isolates the effect of fusion strategy while maintaining the proven effective components, balancing exploitation of current strengths with exploration of key architectural variations.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_033) achieves high accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing resnet50 with a more advanced image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) while keeping RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion consistent could further improve performance. It isolates the effect of the image encoder, leveraging the current top-performing configuration's strengths.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder with scgpt (a more advanced model) could further improve performance, while keeping other components (image encoder, aggregation, fusion) consistent. This comparison isolates the effect of the RNA encoder, which is a critical design choice, and leverages the strong prior evidence for the other components.

The existing evidence shows that using scgpt RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieves the highest validation accuracy of 0.725. This experiment tests the same RNA and image encoders with transformer aggregation but uses concat fusion instead of weighted fusion, isolating the effect of fusion method. It is the best use of the last experiment to validate if the fusion strategy is critical for further improvements.
